text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 3.2% today after oil prices ticked lower on news of Saudi-Iran diplomatic talks aimed at de-escalation in the Middle East. While that might seem counterintuitive, the key context is that crude has already spiked to six-month highs ($115+ Brent) over the past week due to escalating regional tensions and threats to Saudi energy infrastructure. Refiners like Marathon profit when crude prices rise relative to finished product prices (a dynamic called the "crack spread"), and with U.S. refineries running at 93.4% capacity, higher crude costs have already lifted margins; today's modest pullback in oil doesn't erase that week-long surge that benefited the stock.

The stock's 2.8% gain over two weeks reflects the broader benefit to U.S. refiners from the Middle East conflict — tighter global supplies and higher crude prices boost refining profits, especially when domestic demand remains steady. The de-escalation talk today likely triggered some profit-taking in oil itself, but Marathon's strong week-to-date performance and the continued geopolitical premium in prices suggest investors still see tailwinds for refining margins.
